channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Would Charles Schulz Have Done It This Way?
item.description: Pop culture can reveal how much the nicotine debate has changed. A question framed through Charles Schulz and familiar comic-strip nostalgia points to something bigger: public attitudes are shaped as much by stories, humour and moral cues as by evidence. That matters for tobacco harm reduction, because safer nicotine products are often judged through cultural discomfort before their risks are properly compared with smoking. Better public health communication should be clear enough to cut through the cartoon version of the debate. (Published on September 18, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Parliament Matters
item.description: Parliament matters because vaping policy is shaped by the people who decide what evidence is heard, which risks are prioritised and how adult smokers are represented. Poor legislation can make lower-risk products harder to access while cigarettes remain familiar and available. Stronger scrutiny should separate youth protection from adult harm reduction, and enforcement from overreach. The aim should be a legal framework that reduces smoking, supports switching and reflects the real differences between nicotine products. (Published on September 18, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: When Happens When Moral Panic Drives Nicotine Policy? | GFN Interviews #96
item.description: Moral panic makes nicotine policy louder but not smarter. It pushes debate towards fear, urgency and symbolic restriction, while the harder questions about smoking, relative risk and consumer behaviour get pushed aside. The result can be regulation that feels protective but leaves adult smokers with fewer credible routes away from cigarettes. Public health needs evidence, proportion and calm enough to tell the difference between a real risk and a politically useful alarm. (Published on September 18, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Opinion: From habit to health – new paths forward for veterans who smoke
item.description: Veterans who smoke need support that recognises habit, stress, trauma and dependence rather than reducing quitting to willpower. Many have tried to stop before, and some may need lower-risk nicotine options that meet them where they are. Harm reduction can create a more realistic path from habit to health by reducing exposure to combustion while keeping people engaged in care. Better cessation support should be practical, respectful and tailored to the lives of those it aims to help. (Published on September 18, 2026bylinknky.com)
